title: Modular forms — Hecke theory, newforms, and L-functions, Part II: noncongruence subgroups and the unbounded denominators theorem
summary: This continuation develops the arithmetic of weakly holomorphic modular forms on arbitrary finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ). It constructs the modular λ coordinate, compares bounded-denominator and congruence function fields, and plans the Ihara leveraging proof of the unbounded denominators theorem on top of the congruence cohomology of ModularCurvesPartII. Its applications distinguish selected vector-valued components from ambient representations and state the arithmetic-model and differential-module bridges explicitly.
readme:
This continuation develops the arithmetic of weakly holomorphic modular forms on arbitrary finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ). It constructs the modular λ coordinate, compares bounded-denominator and congruence function fields, and plans the Ihara leveraging proof of the unbounded denominators theorem. Its applications distinguish selected vector-valued components from ambient representations and state the arithmetic-model and differential-module bridges explicitly.

This Part II starts with the existing ModularForms character, parity and graded-ring carriers. Its first prerequisite and parent is tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms. Finite-index valence, ordinary cusp boundedness and strict widths are imported library results. Fuchsian quotient and compactification geometry remain with FuchsianOrbifolds. The weakly holomorphic carrier is QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3; congruence classes, the SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) amalgam and congruence subgroup property, the abelian and enhanced Ihara lemmas and the congruence-invariance criterion (CDT §4.5) are ModularCurvesPartII R14.4; the arithmetic holonomy bound is DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendencePartII AA.4; the uniformization of ℂ∖μ_N and its growth estimates are ConformalMappingPartII. They are imported, not planned again.

Conventions: q=exp(πiτ), Q=q², t=q^(1/N), x=λ/16, E={±I}. Weak forms are holomorphic on the upper half-plane and meromorphic at rational cusps. Bounded denominators means one scalar clearing all coefficients. Signed geometric level is distinguished from strict period. The derivative θ_q=(1/πi)d/dτ satisfies θ_qΔ=2E₂Δ. A vector-valued form detects only the span of its values; an ambient representation conclusion requires spanning.

Layers in construction order:
- W1: Weak forms and geometric levels. Characterize weak forms on finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) by meromorphic cusp germs, importing the weakly holomorphic carrier of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3. Pin strict and signed widths, bounded denominators and geometric Wohlfahrt level. Prove intersection, normal-core and p-scaling laws and the signed Wohlfahrt theorem; clear cusp poles by Δ.
- W2: The modular λ coordinate. Construct λ by the existing η function, identify X(2) with ℙ¹ and λ as its three-punctured covering coordinate, prove integral inverse reparametrization and Kummer normalization, and the hypergeometric–theta identity with its character. Connect the N=2 and N=3 punctured-plane acceptance examples.
- W3: Bounded-denominator fields and holonomy rank. Define the ℚ(λ)-spans M₂N and R₂N in rational Laurent series, prove inclusion, multiplication and field structure, construct the normal stabilizer with exact level, place R₂N in the ℚ(λ)-span W of integral holonomic germs for the λ-root coordinate, and derive finiteness and the quantitative rank bound from the corrected holonomic rank theorem of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendencePartII and the uniformization of ℂ∖μ_N of ConformalMappingPartII.
- W4: The nonabelian Ihara lemma and the generation identity. From the principal-level amalgam, the congruence subgroup property of SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) and the enhanced Ihara lemma of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4, prove nonabelian Ihara surjectivity, triple surjectivity on the unsigned domain with its corrected reduction kernel, and the generation identity used by leveraging.
- W5: Leveraging and degree doubling. Establish the field intersection and degree-preserving base change, p-scaling separation, degree doubling, the congruence degree formula and the Chebyshev contradiction.
- W6: The unbounded denominators theorem. Assemble R₂N=M₂N from the rank bound, the ConformalMappingPartII radius and mean-growth estimates and leveraging; reduce arbitrary integral weight to weight zero; deduce congruence from one integral Fourier expansion, its rational bounded-denominator form, and its algebraic-integer form with number-field descent. Verify the j cube root, h roots, and Fermat tests.
- W7: Differential equations and vector-valued forms. Apply the corrected holonomic rank theorem to integral three-point ODE solutions with finite monodromy at zero. Define vector-valued forms and continuation spaces of individual components, build the minimal operator of a component by Wronskians, descend it to ℚ(x), and apply the G-function inputs to componentwise congruence and the corrected effective-span Mason corollary.
- W8: Quasimodular and arithmetic growth applications. Define weakly holomorphic quasimodular forms using E₂ and Δ localization and prove derivative minimality with the q normalization fixed. Verify the elliptic-integral and Catalan identities. Define deficient places and state their congruence and effective arithmetic-component consequences with the necessary detection hypotheses.
- W9: The arithmetic fundamental-group application. On the connected cusp component of the smooth locus of a regular X(N) model, derive the split étale fundamental-group isomorphism from the arithmetic finite-cover criterion and algebraic-integer unbounded denominators; specify model and cover-descent inputs explicitly.

Sources: Calegari–Dimitrov–Tang, The unbounded denominators conjecture, JAMS 38 (2025), pp.627–702, especially Proposition 3.0.1 pp.649–651, §§4.1–4.6 pp.653–666, §6.3 pp.685–686 and applications pp.687–696. Kiming–Schütt–Verrill, arXiv:0905.4798v4, §3 pp.4–6, supplies the signed Wohlfahrt proof. URLs, read boundaries and hashes are in sources.

The definitive target document is research/blueprint/readmes/ModularFormsPartII.md. It states all hypotheses, source matches, APIs and tests. The packet is a complete target-level design pass with all nine stages planned; its five exact input gaps (MODEL, NF, GLOCAL, LOCALGLOBAL, NERON) and request entries remain explicit. No implementation or closed proof plan is claimed. The issue alias ModularFormsPartII implements the extraction route named NoncongruenceModularForms.

stages.title: Weak forms and geometric levels
stages.description:
Characterize weak forms on finite-index subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) by meromorphic cusp germs, importing the weakly holomorphic carrier of QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms QM.3. Pin strict and signed widths, bounded denominators and geometric Wohlfahrt level. Prove intersection, normal-core and p-scaling laws and the signed Wohlfahrt theorem; clear cusp poles by Δ.

**Weak forms on finite-index subgroups: the cusp-germ characterization** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/weak-form`). Let Γ≤SL₂(ℤ) have finite index, regarded in GL₂(ℝ) through the existing coercion, and let k∈ℤ. The space M^!_k(Γ) of weakly holomorphic modular forms is imported from QSeriesPartitionsAndMockModularForms:QM.3/weakly-holomorphic-modular-form: functions holomorphic on ℍ, invariant under the weight-k slash action of Γ, with exponential growth at every cusp. A function f:ℍ→ℂ lies in M^!_k(Γ) if and only if it is holomorphic on ℍ, Γ-invariant, and for every g∈SL₂(ℤ) the slash f|ₖg is periodic with some positive strict period h and its cusp function in q_h is meromorphic at q_h=0, so that its Laurent series has finite principal part. The elements with no negative Laurent term at any cusp are exactly the existing ModularForm Γ k. M^!_k(Γ) is preserved by restriction to a finite-index subgroup, and products add weights. In this roadmap a weak form is an element of M^!_k(Γ) for a finite-index Γ≤SL₂(ℤ), and a weak modular function is the case k=0. Character-valued forms keep the parent character carrier and are not folded into this trivial-character space.

**Bounded denominators of a Fourier germ** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/bounded-denominators`). For an embedded number field K⊆ℂ and a Laurent series a(t)∈K((t)), bounded denominators means there is one nonzero d∈O_K with d a_n∈O_K for every coefficient, including the finite principal part. Over ℚ use one integer D≥1. This is scalar denominator clearing, not substitution t↦t/M. For a holomorphic germ f with positive strict period 2N, its Taylor series is UpperHalfPlane.qExpansion (2N) f in t=e^{πiτ/N}. Integral coefficients mean every coefficient lies in the embedded ℤ, or O_K, as appropriate.

**Geometric Wohlfahrt level** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/wohlfahrt-level`). Write E={±I}, Γᵖ=⟨Γ,E⟩. At g∞ define the signed width wᵍ(Γ) to be the least m>0 with either gT^m g⁻¹ or −gT^m g⁻¹ in Γ. Define L(Γ) as the lcm over the finitely many Γᵖ-cusps of these widths. This equals L(Γᵖ). For E≤Γ, signed width agrees with the existing integerCuspWidth of the conjugate group. Without E≤Γ a strict width may be twice a signed width; odd weights then retain the associated sign in the local parameter.

**Clearing cusp poles with Δ** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/clear-cusp-poles`). For f weak of weight k on finite-index Γ, there exists m≥0 such that fΔ^m is an existing holomorphic ModularForm Γ (k+12m). Multiplication by Δ^m is injective, since Δ has no zero on ℍ. At each cusp the order of Δ is positive. This statement includes irregular cusps and does not assume −I∈Γ.

**Level of an intersection** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/level-intersection`). If E≤G,H and both have finite index, the signed cusp width of G∩H at each rational cusp is lcm(w(G),w(H)); consequently L(G∩H)=lcm(L(G),L(H)). In particular L(G),L(H)∣N implies L(G∩H)∣N.

**Geometric level of the normal core** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/level-normal-core`). For finite-index G≤SL₂(ℤ) containing E, the existing ambient normal core G.normalCore has finite index, contains E, and has exactly L(G).

**Level after p-scaling** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/level-scaling`). Let H contain E, have finite index and L(H)=N. For p prime, A=diag(p,1), set Hᴀ=A⁻¹HA∩SL₂(ℤ). Then Hᴀ has finite index, contains E and L(Hᴀ)∣Np. A does not lie in SL₂(ℤ); conjugation is performed in GL₂(ℚ) before intersection.

**Wohlfahrt’s theorem with signs** (`ModularFormsPartII:W1/wohlfahrt`). If a finite-index congruence G contains E, then Γ(L(G))≤G. For an arbitrary congruence G, the conclusion is Γ(L(G))≤⟨G,E⟩. Thus a congruence subgroup containing E and with geometric level dividing N contains Γ(N).

stages.title: The modular λ coordinate
stages.description:
Construct λ by the existing η function, identify X(2) with ℙ¹ and λ as its three-punctured covering coordinate, prove integral inverse reparametrization and Kummer normalization, and the hypergeometric–theta identity with its character. Connect the N=2 and N=3 punctured-plane acceptance examples.

**The modular λ function** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/lambda`). Using the pinned η on ℂ, set x(τ)=(η(τ/2)η(2τ)²/η(τ)³)^8 and λ(τ)=16x(τ). On ℍ the denominator is nonzero. Pin q=e^{πiτ}: x=q∏_{n≥1}((1+q^{2n})/(1+q^{2n−1}))^8. The associated formal series is the integral q-adic product; agreement with the analytic product is a theorem, not a choice of a formal expansion. Its λ-normalization sends the three Γ(2)-cusps ∞,0,1 to 0,1,∞.

**The λ covering and three cusp values** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/lambda-covering`). λ:ℍ→ℂ∖{0,1} is a holomorphic universal covering with effective deck group Γ(2)/E. It extends to a biholomorphism X(2)≃ℙ¹ sending ∞,0,1 to 0,1,∞. For every finite-index H≤Γ(2) containing E, Y(H)→Y(2) is finite unramified, and the compactified map is branched only above these three values; finite covers are read using the imported covering correspondence.

**The level-two modular-function ring** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/lambda-function-ring`). The ring of complex weight-zero weak forms on Γ(2) is ℂ[λ,λ⁻¹,(1−λ)⁻¹]. Its subring with rational Fourier coefficients at ∞ is ℚ[λ,λ⁻¹,(1−λ)⁻¹]; its fraction field is ℚ(λ). A rational q expansion forces a rational function in λ to have rational coefficients by the integral inverse coordinate and uniqueness of a reduced rational function.

**Integral λ reparametrization** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/inverse-integrality`). The formal x(q)=λ(q)/16 has a unique compositional inverse q(x) in x+x²ℤ[[x]]. Substitution gives mutually inverse ℤ-algebra maps ℤ[[q]]≃ℤ[[x]], and similarly over ℚ and any coefficient ring obtained by scalar extension. Its first terms are q=x+8x²+84x³+992x⁴+12514x⁵ modulo x⁶.

**The normalized Kummer coordinate** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/kummer-coordinate`). For N≥1 and t=q^{1/N}, there is a unique x_N(t)∈t+t²ℚ[[t]] with x_N(t)^N=x(t^N). It belongs to t+t²ℤ[1/N][[t]], and x_N^N is integral. Branches are fixed by x_N/t→1. No claim is made that x_N itself is integral for arbitrary N. Pulling back x=λ/16 by u↦u^N leaves possible singularities at 16^{−1/N}μ_N and ∞; width dividing 2N removes monodromy at u=0.

**Jacobi’s hypergeometric identity with character** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/jacobi-hypergeometric`). Let K₀(x)=Σ_{n≥0}binom(2n,n)²x^n = ₂F₁(1/2,1/2;1;16x). Then K₀(x(τ))=θ₃(τ)². This is weight 1 on Γ(2) with χ(γ)=χ_{−4}(dγ), and is a trivial-character form on H′={γ∈Γ(2):dγ≡1 mod4}. The series is integral and transcendental over ℚ(x); its equation x(1−16x)y″+(1−32x)y′−4y=0 has nontrivial unipotent local monodromy at 0, despite this particular holomorphic branch.

**Two modular uniformization checks** (`ModularFormsPartII:W2/small-uniformizations`). With C(z)=i(1−z)/(1+z), F₂(z)=2λ(C(z))−1 universally covers ℂ∖{±1}, sends 0 to 0, and |F₂′(0)|=Γ(1/4)^4/(4π²)>4. The supplier’s N=3 normalized covering has |F₃′(0)|=Γ(1/6)^3/(12π^{3/2})>16^{1/3}; its η-quotient in Example 5.1.22 agrees with that covering after the chosen rotation. Among N≥2, ℂ∖μ_N is isomorphic to Y(N) only for N=2,3.

stages.title: Bounded-denominator fields and holonomy rank
stages.description:
Define the ℚ(λ)-spans M₂N and R₂N in rational Laurent series, prove inclusion, multiplication and field structure, construct the normal stabilizer with exact level, place R₂N in the ℚ(λ)-span W of integral holonomic germs for the λ-root coordinate, and derive finiteness and the quantitative rank bound from the corrected holonomic rank theorem of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendencePartII and the uniformization of ℂ∖μ_N of ConformalMappingPartII.

**The field M₂N** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/congruence-field`). For N≥1 take t=q^{1/N}, x=λ/16 and the common ambient Laurent field ℚ((t)). M₂N is the ℚ(λ)-linear span of q expansions of weight-zero weak forms on ⟨E,Γ(2N)⟩ with rational coefficients at ∞. Each generating function is holomorphic on Y(2N); poles at cusps are permitted. The embedded ℚ(λ) is specified by the λ series. Its field structure is proved below rather than included as an axiom.

**The field R₂N** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/bounded-field`). Inside the same ℚ((q^{1/N})), R₂N is the ℚ(λ)-linear span of expansions at ∞ of rational-coefficient weight-zero weak forms invariant under some finite-index group H containing E with every cusp width dividing 2N, and having one common denominator. Equivalently choose an admissible H for each generator. A generator can have finitely many negative terms; multiplication by a power of λ makes it holomorphic at ∞ without changing the span. The ℚ(λ)-span itself can introduce interior poles through rational functions of λ.

**Congruence functions have bounded denominators** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/congruence-inclusion`). For all N≥1, M₂N⊆R₂N as subspaces in the specified Laurent field.

**The modular holonomy embedding** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/holonomy-embedding`). For N≥1 let U_N=ℂ∖16^{−1/N}μ_N, t=q^{1/N}, let χ=x_N(t) be the normalized Kummer coordinate of W2/kummer-coordinate and p(u)=u^N, so that p(χ(t))=x(t^N)=λ/16 is integral and ℚ(p)=ℚ(λ). Read through the formal inverse of χ, every element of R₂N lies in the ℚ(p)-span W(U_N,χ,p) of the integral holonomic ring H(U_N,χ,ℤ) of DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendencePartII:AA.4. Each generator enters H after multiplication by a nonzero integer clearing its denominators and by a power of p clearing its pole at ∞; general elements are ℚ(λ)-combinations of these. The containment is in W and not only in the larger ℚ(u)-span V, because χ is not integral for N≥2.

**Finiteness of the bounded-denominator field** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/finite-rank`). For each N≥1, R₂N is finite-dimensional over ℚ(λ). For N≥2 this follows from a holomorphic map φ, defined near the closed unit disc with image in U_N, φ(0)=0 and |φ′(0)|>1. Since R₂⊆R₄ under t↦t², the case N=1 follows from N=2; U₁=ℂ∖{1/16} is not hyperbolic and is not treated by a universal covering.

**The two spans are fields** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/field-structures`). M₂N and R₂N are finite-dimensional ℚ(λ)-subalgebras of the domain ℚ((t)); thus each is a field, with the inclusions ℚ(λ)→M₂N→R₂N injective.

**A normal stabilizer at exact geometric level** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/normal-stabilizer`). There is a normal finite-index subgroup G₂N of SL₂(ℤ) with E≤G₂N≤⟨E,Γ(2N)⟩, L(G₂N)=2N, and every function of R₂N invariant under G₂N. For N=1 the upper group is Γ(2), whose signed level is 2.

**The modular holonomy rank bound** (`ModularFormsPartII:W3/quantitative-rank`). Let F_N:𝔻→ℂ∖μ_N be the normalized coverings of ConformalMappingPartII:U0/roots-cover. Suppose that for all sufficiently large N, |F_N′(0)|≥16^{1/N}(1+A/N³) for some A>0, and that for each fixed B>0 their circle means at r=1−B/N³ satisfy ∫log⁺|F_N(re^{iθ})|dθ/(2π)≤C_B(log N)/N. Then [R₂N:ℚ(λ)]≤C N³ log(2N) for all N≥1, after enlarging C for finitely many small levels.

stages.title: The nonabelian Ihara lemma and the generation identity
stages.description:
From the principal-level amalgam, the congruence subgroup property of SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) and the enhanced Ihara lemma of ModularCurvesPartII R14.4, prove nonabelian Ihara surjectivity, triple surjectivity on the unsigned domain with its corrected reduction kernel, and the generation identity used by leveraging.

**Nonabelian Ihara surjectivity** (`ModularFormsPartII:W4/nonabelian-ihara`). Let N≥3, let E≤G≤⟨E,Γ(N)⟩ with G normal of finite index in SL₂(ℤ) and L(G)=N, and let p∤N be prime. Put S=⟨E,Γ(N)⟩/G, A=diag(p,1), D±=⟨E,Γ(N)⟩∩Γ₀(p) and D=Γ(N)∩Γ₀(p). The map D±→S×S, g↦(gG,AgA⁻¹G), is surjective, and so is its restriction to D. For g∈D± the conjugate AgA⁻¹ lies in ⟨E,Γ(N)⟩ and has upper-right entry divisible by p; conjugation by A does not preserve Γ₀(p).

**Triple surjectivity with the correct kernel** (`ModularFormsPartII:W4/triple-surjectivity`). Under the preceding hypotheses with N≥3, let D=Γ(N)∩Γ₀(p), and let B be the upper triangular subgroup of SL₂(𝔽p). The map D→S×S×B given by the two quotient maps and reduction modulo p is surjective. On this unsigned domain the reduction kernel is Γ(Np).

**The group generation identity** (`ModularFormsPartII:W4/generation`). With N≥3 and the same G,p,A, the subgroup generated by E, G∩Γ(Np), and A⁻¹GA∩Γ₀(p) equals ⟨E,Γ(N)⟩∩Γ₀(p).

stages.title: Leveraging and degree doubling
stages.description:
Establish the field intersection and degree-preserving base change, p-scaling separation, degree doubling, the congruence degree formula and the Chebyshev contradiction.

**Geometric intersection and degree-preserving base change** (`ModularFormsPartII:W5/field-base-change`). For p∤2N, R₂N∩M₂Np=M₂N and [R₂N M₂Np:M₂Np]=[R₂N:M₂N], with every field embedded by the stated q parameter. The second equality is a linear-disjointness assertion; it is not a formal consequence of the intersection for arbitrary extensions.

**p-scaling separates a noncongruence function** (`ModularFormsPartII:W5/scaling-separation`). For N≥1 and p∤2N, if a weight-zero function f∈R₂N is not invariant under any congruence subgroup, then f(pτ) is not in the M₂Np-algebra generated by R₂N. Consequently f(pτ)∈R₂Np supplies a genuinely new field element.

**Degree doubling** (`ModularFormsPartII:W5/degree-doubling`). If [R₂N:M₂N]>1 and p∤2N is prime, then [R₂Np:M₂Np]≥2[R₂N:M₂N].

**The congruence degree comparison** (`ModularFormsPartII:W5/congruence-degree`). For N>1, [M₂N:ℚ(λ)]=(2N)³/12·∏_{p∣2N}(1−p⁻²)>4N³/π². For N=1 the degree is 1. The formula uses the projective index: −I∈Γ(2) and −I∉Γ(2N) for N>1.

**Leveraging contradicts logarithmic normalized degree** (`ModularFormsPartII:W5/leveraging-contradiction`). If [R₂N:ℚ(λ)]≤C N³ log(2N) for a constant C and all N≥1, then R₂N=M₂N for every N.

stages.title: The unbounded denominators theorem
stages.description:
Assemble R₂N=M₂N from the rank bound, the ConformalMappingPartII radius and mean-growth estimates and leveraging; reduce arbitrary integral weight to weight zero; deduce congruence from one integral Fourier expansion, its rational bounded-denominator form, and its algebraic-integer form with number-field descent. Verify the j cube root, h roots, and Fermat tests.

**Equality of the bounded and congruence fields** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/field-equality`). For every N≥1 the embedded fields R₂N and M₂N coincide.

**Integral reduction to weight zero** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/weight-reduction`). Let h₀(τ)=λ(τ)/(16η(τ/2)²). It is holomorphic and nonzero on ℍ, has weight −1 on a congruence subgroup, and its normalized expansion is q^(11/12) times an integral unit with constant term 1. Its inverse has the same integral-unit property after the opposite monomial shift. Thus for any integer k, f↦f h₀^k changes weight k to weight zero on a finite-index group and preserves bounded denominators after enlarging the strict period. A power of λ can clear the remaining pole at ∞.

**The unbounded denominators theorem** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/unbounded-denominators`). Let N≥1, k∈ℤ and Γ≤SL₂(ℤ) have finite index. If f is a weight-k weak form on Γ, holomorphic at ∞ with strict period 2N, and every coefficient of its actual q^{1/N} expansion is in ℤ, then there exists a congruence subgroup Γ′ on which f is a weight-k weak form. Poles at other cusps are allowed.

**Rational bounded denominators force congruence** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/rational-contrapositive`). A rational Fourier expansion of a weak modular form, with one common denominator and a finite principal part, belongs to a congruence weak form. Equivalently a rational-coefficient weak form that is not invariant under any congruence subgroup has unbounded denominators at every cusp where its expansion is rational.

**Algebraic-integer Fourier coefficients** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/number-field-variant`). If a weak modular form of integer weight has an expansion at ∞ in O_K[[q^{1/N}]] for a number field K⊆ℂ, then it is a congruence weak form. The same conclusion holds for an expansion in the algebraic integers Q̄ with the common-number-field and conjugation bridge NF supplied. One scalar denominator over O_K and finitely many negative exponents are also allowed.

**The integral cube root of j** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/j-cube-root`). In the standard parameter Q=e^{2πiτ}, the branch j^(1/3)=E₄/η⁸=Q^(−1/3)(1+248Q+4124Q²+34752Q³+⋯) has integral Laurent coefficients and is a weak modular function on a level-3 congruence subgroup. Multiplying it by Δ brings it within the holomorphic-at-∞ hypothesis of W6.

**The h-root denominator test** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/h-root-test`). Set h=λ(1−λ)/16=q∏_{n≥1}((1+q^{2n})/(1+q^n))^{24}=q∏_{m odd}(1+q^m)^{−24}. It is a nowhere-vanishing weak modular function for the theta group ⟨Γ(2),S⟩, the conjugate of Γ₀(2) containing S. For n≥1, the branch h^{1/n} with leading term q^{1/n} has bounded denominators if and only if n∣24, and is a congruence weak modular function if and only if n∣24.

**The Fermat-cover test** (`ModularFormsPartII:W6/fermat-test`). The cover u^n+v^n=1 above λ=u^n, for n≥1, is congruence precisely for n∈{1,2,4,8}. Its normalized branch (1−16x)^(1/n), x=λ/16, has bounded denominators precisely for those n.

stages.title: Differential equations and vector-valued forms
stages.description:
Apply the corrected holonomic rank theorem to integral three-point ODE solutions with finite monodromy at zero. Define vector-valued forms and continuation spaces of individual components, build the minimal operator of a component by Wronskians, descend it to ℚ(x), and apply the G-function inputs to componentwise congruence and the corrected effective-span Mason corollary.

**Algebraicity for integral three-point ODE solutions** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/ode-algebraicity`). Let f∈ℤ[[x]] solve a nonzero linear differential operator over ℚ̄(x), with no genuine singularities outside {0,1/16,∞}, and with finite local monodromy at 0 in the supplier’s meromorphic-after-finite-ramification sense. Apparent singularities are allowed only when every local solution is meromorphic. Then f is algebraic over ℚ(x). In the regular-singular case the stated finite-monodromy condition is the usual finite-order local monodromy condition.

**The congruence refinement for ODE solutions** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/ode-congruence`). Under W7/ode-algebraicity, the distinguished continuation f(λ(τ)/16) is invariant under Γ(M) for some M≥1. If the scalar solution has apparent poles on ℍ, it is a meromorphic congruence modular function; if it has none, it is weakly holomorphic.

**Vector-valued modular forms** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/vector-valued-form`). For n≥0, k∈ℤ, a vector-valued form consists of ρ:PSL₂(ℤ)→GL_n(ℂ) and a holomorphic F:ℍ→ℂⁿ with F|ₖγ=ρ(γ)F after pullback to SL₂(ℤ), semisimple ρ(T), and the following growth: for every real a<b and C>0 there are A,B>0 such that each |F_j(τ)|≤A exp(B Im τ) when a≤Re τ≤b and Im τ≥C. Since ρ(−I)=1, nonzero such forms have even weight. The SL₂ version with central character is a separate imported parity convention.

**Generalized Fourier expansions without logarithms** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/generalized-expansion`). In a basis diagonalizing ρ(T), each component has a convergent expansion Q^μ Σ_{m≥m₀}a_m Q^m, Q=e^{2πiτ}, where exp(2πiμ) is its T-eigenvalue and μ may be complex. Conversely such expansions with finite lower support give the required moderate exponential strip growth. There are no logarithms; rational exponents or finite-order T are not asserted.

**Inducing a scalar weak form** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/induced-scalar`). For E≤Γ of finite index and even k, a weak scalar form on Γ yields a vector-valued form with finite-image coset permutation representation, whose components are f|ₖγ for coset representatives and whose identity component is f. For groups excluding E or odd weight use the parent SL₂ central-character convention.

**The complex local system of ρ** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/complex-local-system`). For a weight-zero vector-valued form, let L_ρ be the rank-n complex local system on Y(2)=ℙ¹∖{0,1/16,∞} associated to ρ restricted to Γ(2)/E. Build it by descent of the trivial bundle on ℍ with its flat connection. It has this specified rank independently of linear relations between component functions. This does not define an integral free module or an arithmetic connection.

**The continuation space of a component** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/component-continuation`). For a fixed weight-zero component f=F_j, let W_j be the complex vector space of its analytic continuation germs at a fixed ordinary point of Y(2). The slash transformation expresses each branch as a constant linear combination of the n component functions, so dim W_j≤n. Use the resulting monodromy subquotient of L_ρ, retaining the actual scalar germ and all its linear relations. Do not assert irreducibility.

**The minimal operator of a component germ** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/regular-singular-component`). With x=λ/16, the continuation space W_j of a weight-zero component f=F_j is the full solution space, at an ordinary point, of a unique monic operator L_j∈ℂ(x)[∂] of order dim W_j. L_j is the minimal operator of the germ f. It is regular singular, has no genuine singularities outside {0,1/16,∞}, and has apparent singularities only at points of ℍ where all its local solutions are holomorphic. Its local monodromies are those of W_j, hence semisimple.

**Arithmetic descent and finite component monodromy** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/arithmetic-component`). If the selected weight-zero component has an integral x-series f∈ℤ[[x]], then its minimal operator L_j has coefficients in ℚ(x), f is a G-function, the companion system of L_j satisfies Galochkin's condition, L_j is globally nilpotent and its local monodromies are quasi-unipotent. Together with semisimplicity, every local monodromy of W_j has finite order.

**Arithmetic normalization of a vector-valued component** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/vv-weight-normalization`). For a nonzero even-weight vector-valued form of weight k, choose an integral scalar congruence form g of weight k′≥0 with 12∣k+k′. Multiply F by g·(λ/(16Δ(τ/2)))^((k+k′)/12), choosing the branch with leading term 1. This has weight zero after restriction to a finite congruence cover, preserves an integral selected Fourier germ, and has only finite-order additional monodromy. Division back recovers congruence of the original selected component.

**Congruence of an integral vector-valued component** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/component-congruence`). Let (F,ρ) be as defined above and let F_j have an actual expansion in ℤ[[q]], q=e^{πiτ}. Then F_j is a classical weight-k weak form on some Γ(M). No assertion is made about an unused summand of ρ.

**Mason’s corollary on the effective value span** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/effective-mason`). Suppose each component of F becomes an integral Fourier series after multiplication by a nonzero scalar and enlargement of its strict period. Put V_F=span_ℂ{F(τ):τ∈ℍ}. Then V_F is ρ-stable and Γ(M) acts identically on V_F for some M. If V_F=ℂⁿ, ker ρ contains Γ(M) and ρ has finite image. Without spanning, the conclusion applies only to ρ|V_F.

**An invisible infinite-image summand** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/invisible-summand-test`). Set σ(S)=diag(1,−1), σ(R)=[[2,1],[−7,−3]] for the presentation PSL₂(ℤ)=⟨S,R:S²=R³=1⟩, and T=SR. Then σ(T)=[[2,1],[7,3]] is semisimple of infinite order. The pair ρ=1⊕σ, F=(1,0,0), k=0 satisfies the vector-valued definition with integral coefficients but ρ has infinite image.

**Positive-weight forms and infinite monodromy** (`ModularFormsPartII:W7/stiller-zagier`). Let h be a nonzero congruence form of positive integer weight k, modular on Γ′, and express it as a germ in x=λ/16 on the finite étale cover Y(Γ′∩Γ(2))→Y(2). Its continuation space is spanned by τ^i h for 0≤i≤k, so its minimal operator has order exactly k+1. The monodromy on this space is Sym^k of the standard representation, has infinite image, and is unipotent and nontrivial at every cusp. Apparent singularities on ℍ occur exactly at the zeros of h. If h has an actual expansion in ℤ[[q]], integral inverse λ reparametrization gives an integral x-series; for a fractional q-expansion the corresponding Puiseux germ is retained, and integrality after a fractional change is not asserted without checking its unit root.

stages.title: Quasimodular and arithmetic growth applications
stages.description:
Define weakly holomorphic quasimodular forms using E₂ and Δ localization and prove derivative minimality with the q normalization fixed. Verify the elliptic-integral and Catalan identities. Define deficient places and state their congruence and effective arithmetic-component consequences with the necessary detection hypotheses.

**Weakly holomorphic quasimodular forms** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/weak-quasimodular`). For a finite-index Γ≤SL₂(ℤ), use its integral-weight modular-form ring M(Γ) from the parent, retaining its central-character convention. If E≤Γ, only even weights contribute. Set M̃(Γ)=M(Γ)[E₂] and M̃!(Γ)=M̃(Γ)[Δ⁻¹] inside holomorphic functions on ℍ. Equivalently M̃!=M!(Γ)[E₂]. Weights and quasimodular depth are retained as filtrations. The existing E₂ is used; this is not a new definition of the Eisenstein series.

**The differential ring generated by weak forms** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/derivative-minimality`). With θ_q=(1/πi)d/dτ and q=e^{πiτ}, M̃!(Γ) is the smallest ℂ-subalgebra of holomorphic functions on ℍ containing M!(Γ) and closed under θ_q. In this normalization θ_qΔ=2E₂Δ, so E₂=(θ_qΔ)/(2Δ). For D=(1/2πi)d/dτ, DΔ=E₂Δ.

**The elliptic integral of the second kind** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/elliptic-integral-test`). Let K₀(x)=Σ binom(2n,n)²x^n and E₀(x)=₂F₁(−1/2,1/2;1;16x). Then E₀=(1−16x)K₀+8∫₀ˣK₀(t)dt. At x=λ/16, E₀=(θ₃θ₄⁴+4θ_qθ₃)/θ₃³ belongs to M̃!(Γ(12)) and has q-series 1−4q+20q²−64q³+164q⁴−392q⁵+⋯.

**Catalan integral and theta quotient checks** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/catalan-tests`). The series I₁(x)=Σ binom(2n,n)²x^(n+1)/(n+1) and I₂(x)=Σ C_n²x^(n+1), C_n=binom(2n,n)/(n+1), are integral. Their derivatives satisfy I₁′=K₀ and xI₂′=I₁. Moreover Σ C_n²(λ/16)^n=(4/θ₂⁴)(4θ₃² θ_qθ₂/θ₂+4θ₃ θ_qθ₃−θ₃⁴) belongs to M̃!(Γ(12)).

**Cuspidal arithmetic components and deficient places** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/deficient-places`). Fix a number field K⊆ℂ and a representation ρ. Let S_k(ρ;K) be the K-space of cuspidal vector-valued forms whose components have actual expansions in tK[[t]] for t=q^(1/N), some common N. A normalized place v of K is deficient if some such component Σ_{m≥1}a_m t^m has unbounded |a_m|_v at a finite v, or unbounded |a_m|_v/m^((k−1)/2+ε) for some ε>0 at an archimedean v. An archimedean place uses its usual modulus, not its square. The source's version is K=ℚ; the number-field version specializes to it.

**Congruence kernels have no deficient places** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/congruence-no-deficiency`). If ker ρ contains a principal congruence subgroup, then every Σ_K(ρ) is empty. At finite places a common scalar denominator bounds the coefficients. At every archimedean place the coefficients of a weight-k cuspidal component satisfy |a_m|≪_ε m^((k−1)/2+ε) for every ε>0.

**A finite deficient place from an arithmetic witness** (`ModularFormsPartII:W8/noncongruence-witness`). Let a cuspidal component f over K be noncongruence. If its coefficient denominators are supported on a finite set S of finite places, then at least one v∈S is deficient. More generally the same conclusion follows from a supplied local-to-global denominator theorem for this component class. Thus an ambient representation conclusion additionally needs arithmetic forms detecting its noncongruence effective representation. These two hypotheses are not omitted.

stages.title: The arithmetic fundamental-group application
stages.description:
On the connected cusp component of the smooth locus of a regular X(N) model, derive the split étale fundamental-group isomorphism from the arithmetic finite-cover criterion and algebraic-integer unbounded denominators; specify model and cover-descent inputs explicitly.

**The connected cuspal smooth model** (`ModularFormsPartII:W9/cuspal-model`). For N≥1 and a finite extension K/ℚ(μ_N), start with a minimal regular model of X(N) over O_K and the extension ε of its rational ∞ cusp. Let 𝒳_cusp(N) denote the smooth open selecting the connected fibre component through ε at each finite place, with the same generic fibre. Require existence, uniqueness and compatibility of this selection as the model contract NERON. This pins the intended connected Néron model; it does not confuse a global connected component of an irreducible total space with a component in each fibre.

**The arithmetic finite-cover criterion** (`ModularFormsPartII:W9/arithmetic-cover-criterion`). Every finite étale cover of 𝒳_cusp(N) is the pullback of a finite étale cover of Spec O_K, with morphisms descending uniquely. This statement includes all primes dividing N. It is the precise arithmetic geometric input to the fundamental-group theorem.

**The fundamental group of the connected cuspal model** (`ModularFormsPartII:W9/arithmetic-pi1`). For N≥1, K/ℚ(μ_N) finite and every geometric η of Spec O_K, the maps π_*:π₁(𝒳_cusp(N),ε(η))→π₁(Spec O_K,η) and ε_* in the opposite direction are mutually inverse isomorphisms.
